legal_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me generate a mutual NDA document from a template as the first step in sending an NDA to a potential partner or vendor. Before starting, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: (1) my company's full legal name and state/country of incorporation, (2) the counterparty's full legal name and entity type, (3) the effective date for the NDA, (4) the intended purpose/scope of the confidential relationship (e.g., 'evaluating a potential partnership in X'), (5) the governing law/jurisdiction I want to use, (6) the term length and any post-termination confidentiality survival period, and (7) whether I have a preferred NDA template on file (in a document store, drive, or shared folder) or want you to use a standard mutual NDA structure.

Once you have these inputs, draft a complete mutual NDA document that includes: parties and recitals, definition of confidential information, obligations of both parties, exclusions from confidentiality, term and termination, remedies, governing law, and signature blocks for both parties. Fill in all placeholders with the specific details I provided, and clearly flag any fields you could not fill in (mark them as [NEEDS INPUT]).

Save the draft as a new document (e.g., in Google Docs, a shared drive, or as a file) and share the location/link with me. Do not send it to the counterparty or move to the signature step yet — this step only covers generating the draft.

When done, report back: the document link/location, a summary of key terms filled in, and a list of any fields still needing my input before it's ready to send.

legal_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a mutual NDA for review before it's sent to a potential partner or vendor. This is a preparation-only task: you will flag issues for my judgment, but final approval of legal terms must come from me or our counsel.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) our standard/template NDA text (or confirm if we don't have one and need to use a generic mutual NDA baseline), (2) the counterparty's name and any NDA draft they've sent (if this is their version instead of ours), (3) key deal context — what confidential information will be shared, expected duration of the relationship, and our target term length and jurisdiction preferences.

Then review the draft and produce a structured summary covering:
- Definition of Confidential Information — scope, and any unusual exclusions/carve-outs
- Term/duration of confidentiality obligations and whether it's mutual
- Governing law and jurisdiction
- Any non-standard clauses (non-solicitation, IP assignment, indemnification, residual knowledge clauses) that go beyond a typical mutual NDA
- Any deviations from our standard template if one was provided, listed clause-by-clause
- Red flags: one-sided obligations, unusually long terms (e.g., over 3-5 years), broad indemnification, or missing mutuality

Format this as a clear markdown table or list: Clause | Standard/Expected | What This Draft Says | Flag (yes/no) | Notes.

Do not approve, redline, sign, or send the NDA yourself, and do not tell the counterparty anything has been accepted. Your output is a review memo only. End your report with a clear statement that this requires human legal judgment and should stop for human sign-off before any terms are approved or the document is sent.

legal_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare and stage a mutual NDA for e-signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform, but you must NOT actually dispatch it — a human must approve before anything is sent.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) the partner/vendor company's legal name, signer name, title, and email; (2) our company's legal name, signer name, title, and email; (3) the NDA template or draft text to use (or confirm you should use our standard mutual NDA template if one exists in our files); (4) effective date and any deal-specific terms (confidentiality term length, jurisdiction, exclusions) I want inserted.

Then: populate the NDA document with both parties' details and terms, verify all placeholder fields are filled and both signature blocks are correctly assigned, and prepare a new envelope in {{vendor}} using its documented API or dashboard — set the document, signer names/emails, signing order/routing, and any signature-field placement, exactly as you would for a real send, but do NOT finalize or transmit the envelope.

Done looks like: a fully populated NDA ready for signature, an {{vendor}} envelope created in draft/pending state with correct recipients and routing configured, and a clear summary of what will happen when sent (who signs in what order, expiration/reminder settings if applicable).

Report back to me with: the finalized NDA text or a link/reference to it, the envelope's current draft status in {{vendor}}, the recipient/routing configuration, and any fields you were unsure about. Then stop for human sign-off — do not click send, submit, or finalize the envelope yourself under any circumstances.

legal_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track the signature status of a mutual NDA that was already sent for signature through {{vendor}}. Since this is an asynchronous process, please note that the result won't be immediate — you'll need to check status now and then verify again later rather than expecting instant completion.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need: the {{vendor}} account/workspace details (use my configured credentials to access it), the name of the recipient/partner the NDA was sent to, and the envelope or document identifier if I have one.

Once you have what you need:
1. Use the {{vendor}} dashboard or API to check the current status of the NDA envelope (e.g., sent, viewed, signed, declined, expired).
2. If {{vendor}} supports webhooks, check whether an event subscription exists for status changes on this envelope; if not, set one up or note that this should be configured so future status changes are pushed automatically instead of requiring manual polling.
3. Confirm whether signing order, reminders, and an expiration date are set on the outstanding request, and flag if any are missing.
4. If the envelope is fully signed, retrieve the tamper-evident audit trail and completion certificate and save/note their location.
5. If still pending, note the current signer, time elapsed, and when you plan to re-check.

Done looks like: you've reported the current signature status, confirmed whether webhook-based monitoring is active (or set it up), verified reminder/expiration settings, and — if complete — retrieved the audit trail and certificate.

Report back with: the envelope's current status, who has/hasn't signed, whether automated event monitoring is in place, any reminder/expiration settings found, and next steps or a re-check time if the NDA is still outstanding. If final signature is not yet complete, remind me this remains a step you'll need to poll or verify again later.

legal_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me file the fully executed NDA into our cloud storage system, {{vendor}}. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (a) the signed/executed NDA file (PDF or equivalent), (b) the target folder or parent folder ID in {{vendor}} where legal documents are stored, and (c) any naming convention I want used (e.g., "NDA_[PartnerName]_[Date].pdf").

2. Confirm my configured {{vendor}} credentials are active, then upload the executed NDA file into the specified folder. For smaller files, use a simple upload call such as POST /upload/drive/v3/files?uploadType=media; for larger files, use a resumable flow such as POST /upload/drive/v3/files?uploadType=resumable, or the equivalent PUT /me/drive/items/{parent-id}:/{filename}:/content and POST /me/drive/items/{item-id}:/createUploadSession calls, matching whichever endpoint style is appropriate for {{vendor}}.

3. After upload, set custom metadata/properties on the file (e.g., document type = "NDA", counterparty name, execution date, status = "executed") using {{vendor}}'s metadata schema capability, so the file is queryable later.

4. Verify the upload succeeded by listing the file and confirming it appears in the target folder with the correct name and metadata. Also confirm version history is enabled/retained for this file per {{vendor}}'s retention window, in case a revision needs to be restored later.

5. Report back to me with: the file's location/path or link in {{vendor}}, the metadata values you set, and confirmation that the upload and metadata write both completed successfully. Flag any errors or permission issues you encounter instead of retrying indefinitely.
